cards.title: Reflectivity-dependent HOM visibility

checks.reason: The supplement defines distinguishable and indistinguishable coincidence probabilities.
Visibility is one at R=1/2 and zero at R=0 or 1.
Printed endpoint reconstruction gives 0.9696 for fiber and 0.9998 for LNOI, preserving the reported ordering.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate monochromatic or spectrum-weighted visibility for any reflectivity curve.
open_questions: The measured reflectivity and grating-response arrays are unavailable.

cards.title: Gaussian HOM delay model and bandwidth conventions

source_refs.value: Main Fig. 4(b): visibility 0.832 and width 71.9 fs

checks.reason: The main text prints the dip visibility and fitted width but not the exact width convention.
At |tau|=w/2 the Gaussian envelope is exactly one half.
The 0.441 Gaussian convention maps 71.9 fs to 49.92 nm, while the HOM autocorrelation convention maps it to 70.64 nm; both are retained.

cards.numerical_form: Generate the fitted curve and report several explicit Gaussian time-bandwidth conventions.
open_questions: The paper does not say whether 71.9 fs is FWHM, sigma, or another reported width convention.

cards.title: Two-photon loss-corrected source brightness

source_refs.value: Main text: >5800 pairs/s, about 13 dB loss per photon, about 10 uW pump

checks.reason: All three rounded scalar inputs are printed in the main text.
5800 detections/s, 13 dB loss per photon, and 10 uW pump give 2.309e8 pairs/s/mW.

cards.numerical_form: Apply loss independently to both detected photons before dividing by pump power.
open_questions: The detector rate and pump power are printed as inequalities or approximate values.

cards.title: Scalar waveguide mode and electrode-overlap loss reconstruction

source_refs.value: Main Fig. 1(c), printed cross-section dimensions, and Supplement Fig. S7

cards.latex: [-nabla_t^2-k0^2 n(x,y)^2]E=-beta^2 E; alpha proportional to integral_metal |E|^2 dA

checks.reason: The paper states finite-element mode solving and shows the declared geometry; full solver settings are absent.
The scalar finite-difference solve returns guided effective indices 1.98194 at 781 nm and 1.67882 at 1562 nm with normalized intensities.
The perturbative metal-overlap loss decreases monotonically as the electrode gap grows.

cards.numerical_form: Use a finite-difference scalar Helmholtz solve and an explicitly declared evanescent metal-overlap model.
open_questions: Exact sidewall angle, material dispersion table, electrode thickness, and vector boundary conditions are not published.
